extracted.intended_audience: readers of tech media, journalists, editors, and media-ethics observers
extracted.subtask_description: Identifying standards and failure modes for AI-generated news articles (accuracy, originality, disclosure, legal and editorial controls) to evaluate or guide the publication of such content. Focused on online news sites using generative AI for article production.

rubrics_metrics.name: Disclosure of AI use
rubrics_metrics.description: Publishers must disclose when articles are AI-generated; the page reports CNET was "caught quietly publishing AI-generated articles without disclosing the development to readers."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Transparency to readers about use of AI is required — do not publish AI-generated stories without an explicit disclosure explaining that the content was produced or substantially assisted by AI.

rubrics_metrics.name: Accuracy / factual correctness
rubrics_metrics.description: AI-generated pieces contained a "multitude of errors... discovered in the bot’s work."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure fact-checking and verification processes for AI output; do not publish content with unchecked factual errors. Implement accuracy controls comparable to human-written journalism.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid plagiarism / ensure originality
rubrics_metrics.description: Articles "were stitched together by stealing bits from other media outlets, swapping words with synonyms to create the illusion that they were original ideas."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not piece together text from other outlets without proper transformation and attribution. Beware of superficial paraphrasing (synonym-swapping) as an anti-pattern that produces the illusion of originality while still copying others’ work.

rubrics_metrics.name: Proper sourcing and attribution
rubrics_metrics.description: The reporting describes content "lifting more or less word for word from existing stories," indicating unattributed reuse of other outlets’ material.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Attribute source material clearly and avoid unattributed borrowing. Maintain provenance metadata and citations for facts, quotes, and reporting sourced (even indirectly) via AI.

rubrics_metrics.name: Training/data provenance and model behavior transparency
rubrics_metrics.description: A quoted expert said the AI "was not drawing from the entirety of the internet and carefully coming up with a new mosaic, but rather just lifting more or less word for word from existing stories."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Be transparent about the model’s training/data sources and assess whether the model synthesizes information or reproduces training examples. Use models and data practices that minimize verbatim reproduction of copyrighted texts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Legal and copyright compliance
rubrics_metrics.description: The article notes the site was "embroiled in potential legal trouble" when plagiarism was discovered in AI output.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Verify that published content does not infringe copyright or other legal rights. Put legal review and clearance processes in place for AI-generated material to reduce exposure to lawsuits or takedown claims.

rubrics_metrics.name: Editorial oversight and operational safeguards
rubrics_metrics.description: Following the revelations, "The site announced on Friday that it will halt the use of AI to artificially generate stories 'for now.'"
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Require human editorial review of AI-produced drafts before publication; maintain policies to pause, audit, and remediate AI usage when issues arise. Establish clear operational guidelines for when and how AI may be employed in reporting.
